I am 50 years old, and I have worked my 7 mu in Quzhou County for 35 years. I only went to primary school, so I did not learn farming from books. My father taught me, and now I learn by watching what my neighbors do and listening to the seed dealer in town. My wife and I are the only two in our household, so we do most of the work ourselves.

For my 4 mu of chili-cabbage rotation, that is where I make my real money. Last year my chili yielded about 5,000 jin per mu, and I want to keep it there. I buy hybrid chili seeds from the shop — about 80 yuan for the 4 mu — and transplant in late April. For fertilizer, I put down one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu as a base, then topdress twice with urea and once with potassium sulfate. In total that comes to about 22 kg of nitrogen per mu. I know fertilizer is expensive — a bag of compound is 180 yuan now — but my neighbor Old Zhang tried to save money on chili fertilizer two years ago and his yield dropped by half. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I irrigate from my well about 12 times through the season, and I spray pesticide 8 times because aphids and whiteflies always come. After the chili comes off in September, I rotary-till that same 4 mu and plant hybrid cabbage using seedlings I buy from the dealer. Cabbage gets a bit less fertilizer — about 18 kg nitrogen per mu — and 8 irrigations. I spray 5 times for caterpillars. If the frost holds off, I should get 10,000 jin per mu.

My other 2 mu I plant summer maize in June. Maize is easier. I plough the field and sow hybrid seed — 5 jin per mu. I spread half a bag of compound per mu and a little urea, about 15 kg nitrogen total. I irrigate 4 times and spray twice for armyworm. I expect 1,200 jin per mu.

The last 1 mu I sow spinach in October. I use improved spinach seed — 6 jin for the mu. Spinach does not need much: about 10 kg nitrogen per mu from half a bag of compound and some urea. I irrigate 5 times and spray pesticide twice. Should get about 3,600 jin per mu if the winter is not too harsh.

I watch every yuan. For the whole farm I need about 18 bags of compound fertilizer and 10 bags of urea — that is over 4,000 yuan right there. Add seeds, pesticide, and electricity for the pump, and my input cost is about 7,000 yuan. During chili transplanting I hire two workers for three days at 150 yuan per day each because my wife and I cannot do it alone. That is another 900 yuan. I think about my whole budget. If I spend too much on maize fertilizer, I have less for chili, and chili is my cash crop, so chili gets fed first. When I am unsure, I do what I did last year. Change is risky.
